hook.line: Day one of explaining SEO; the best tip is the last one, so stick around.
hook.visual: Close face in a black cap with a clip-on light, finger pointed at the lens; white box title 'Day 1: SEO for beginners/ business owners' at top, small caption pill below.

beats.what: Day 1 series title over a close talking head, finger to the lens
Jump cut on 'best tip is the last one', the open loop that holds to the end
Cut to phone footage of his monitor: Google search for plumbers in Boston
Number one, reviews: scrolls the map pack listing
Reviews panel; caption reads out '26 minutes ago, 2 days ago' as proof of frequency
Back to face for number two, the primary category story
Cut to the business profile on screen, finger pointing at 364 photos
Finger taps phone number and appointment link lines on the monitor
Number four: profile posts, finger points at keywords and location
Face: see you for day two

why_it_works: Saying the best tip is last creates an open loop that pays off at 79 s
A real competitor's profile is the example, so every tip is shown on screen rather than described
A finger physically pointing at the monitor works as an arrow without any graphics
Day 1 framing promises a series, so the end line doubles as a reason to follow
weaknesses: Phone-filmed monitor footage is shaky and glare-prone; small text is hard to read
Small caption pill in thin font is easy to miss
Quiet mix (-29 LUFS) compared with typical feed audio
for_robert: Steal the open loop: say up front that the best tip is last, and have Fred visibly guard a closed box until the final tip, opening it at the payoff.
